questions.question: The value of an Apple laptop depreciated from Rs. 1,33,100 to Rs. 72,900 in 3 years. Find the yearly rate of depreciation. (Correct to 2 decimal places.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Final Value to Initial Value = 72900 ÷ 133100 = 729 ÷ 1331

For a period of 3 years, take the cube root of the ratio: ³√(729) ÷ ³√(1331) = 9 ÷ 11

This means the value of the laptop drops from 11 parts to 9 parts in one year.

Yearly Depreciation % = [(11 − 9) ÷ 11] × 100 = (2 ÷ 11) × 100

Depreciation % = 18.18%

**∴ The correct answer is 18.18%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7631fb701f4d181f95af2e5cb277b3b5821536e0a818964bd135c948c5963ee6.png] 

**Given:**

Initial Value (P) = Rs. 1,33,100

Final Value (A) = Rs. 72,900

Time (n) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

A = P × (1 − R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ 72900 = 133100 × (1 − R/100)³

⇒ 72900 ÷ 133100 = (1 − R/100)³

⇒ 729 ÷ 1331 = (1 − R/100)³

⇒ (9 ÷ 11)³ = (1 − R/100)³

⇒ 9 ÷ 11 = 1 − R/100

⇒ R/100 = 1 − (9 ÷ 11)

⇒ R/100 = 2 ÷ 11

⇒ R = 200 ÷ 11

⇒ R = 18.1818... ≈ 18.18%

**∴ The correct answer is 18.18%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Depreciation Formula

Depreciation represents a consistent percentage decrease over time and follows the compound interest formula with a negative rate: A = P(1 − R/100)ⁿ.

Appreciation Formula

When an asset's value increases annually (like population growth), use the standard compound interest formula: A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ.

Effective Rate of Successive Depreciation

For two consecutive years with the same depreciation rate R, the net effective depreciation percentage is given by: 2R − R²/100.
</p

questions.question: In a mixture of 624 litres, the ratio of milk and water is 5 ∶ 3. The amount of water to be further added to the mixture so as to make the ratio of the milk to water 5 ∶ 4 will be:
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Initial 624 litres

Initial ratio of milk to water: 5 ∶ 3

Desired ratio of milk to water: 5 ∶ 4

**Concept: **

To keep the amount of milk constant, calculate the amount of water that needs to be added to achieve the desired ratio.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Volume of milk = 5 / (5 + 3) x 624 litres = 390 litres

⇒ Volume of water in new mixture = 4 / 5 x 390 litres = 312 litres

⇒ Volume of water to be added = (3 / (5 + 3) x 624 litres) - 312 = 78 litres

**Therefore, 78 litres of water needs to be added to achieve the desired ratio.**

questions.question: A man sold two pens at Rs. 12 each. On one, he gained 20% and on the other, he lost 20%. On the whole, he:
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Selling price of each pen: Rs. 12

Gain on first pen: 20%

Loss on second pen: 20%

**Concept:**

Cost Price = 100 × SP/(100 ± Profit%/Loss%)

Loss = CP - SP

**Calculation:**

SP of each pen = Rs. 12

Gain on first pen: 20%

⇒ CP₁ = 100 × 12/(100 + 20)

⇒ CP1 = Rs. 10

Loss on second pen: 20%

⇒ CP2 = 100 × 12/(100 - 20)

⇒ CP2 = Rs. 15

⇒ Total CP = 10 + 15 = Rs. 25

⇒ Total SP = 12 + 12 = Rs.24

Loss = CP - SP 

⇒ 25 - 24 = Rs. 1

**Therefore, On the whole, he lost Rs. 1.**

questions.question: Two trains of same length are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions with speeds of 54 km/h and 90 km/h respectively. They cross each other in 12 sec. Find the length (in metres) of each train.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (opposite direction) = 54 + 90 = 144 km/h.

Speed in m/s = 144 × (5 ÷ 18) = 40 m/s.

Total distance covered in 12 sec = 40 × 12 = 480 m.

Since both trains have the same length, length of one train = 480 ÷ 2 = 240 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 240 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c7b8e1499bcaad78f9d420850a1cf321564ebf396e708d80545a1506db28918.png] 

**Given:**

Speed of first train (S₁) = 54 km/h

Speed of second train (S₂) = 90 km/h

Time taken to cross each other = 12 sec

Let the length of each train be 'L' metres.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

In opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 54 + 90 = 144 km/h

⇒ Convert km/h to m/s: 144 × (5 ÷ 18) = 40 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = Length of Train 1 + Length of Train 2 = L + L = 2L

⇒ 2L = 40 × 12

⇒ 2L = 480

⇒ L = 240

**∴ The correct answer is 240 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂. When moving in the same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Train Crossing Objects

The distance covered when crossing a stationary point (pole or man) is the length of the train itself. When crossing a platform or another train, the total distance is the sum of both lengths.

Speed Conversions

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by (5 ÷ 18). To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by (18 ÷ 5).
</p

questions.question: The Time taken by Anjali to finish a piece of work is four times the time taken by Ron and Three times the time taken by John. If all three of them work together, it takes them 4 days to complete the entire work. How much time Ron alone take to finish the work?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Time taken by Anjali to finish work is 4 times the time taken by Ron and 3 times the time taken by John.

Time taken by all three working together = 4 days

**Concept: **

The reciprocal of the time taken by each person equals the work done by them per day. The sum of their work per day equals the reciprocal of the time taken by them working together.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let time taken by Ron be x days.

⇒ Therefore, time taken by Anjali = 4x days, time taken by John = 4/3x days

⇒ Work done by Ron per day = 1/x, by Anjali = 1/4x, by John = 3/4x

⇒ Total work done per day = 1/x + 1/4x + 3/4x = 1/4

⇒ (4 + 1 + 3)/4x = 1/4

⇒ 8/4x = 1/4

⇒ Solving for x gives x = 8

**Therefore, Ron takes 8 days to finish the work alone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** 

Time ∝ 1/Efficiecny

days → Anjali : Ron

 4 : 1

So

Efficiency → Anjali : Ron

 1 : 4

same as,

days → Anjali : John

 3 : 1

So

Efficiency → Anjali : John

 1 : 3

So

Efficiency → Anjali : Ron : John

 1 : 4 : 3

So

Total work = Total days * Total efficiency 

Total work = 4 * (1 + 4 + 3) = 32 units

days required to Ron to complete the work = 32/4 **= 8 days**

questions.question: Calculate the cost to paint a water tank in the shape of a sphere having a radius of 7 cm, if the cost of painting is Rs.4.5/cm² . (π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Surface Area of Sphere = 4 × π × r²

Total Area = 4 × (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 616 cm²

Total Cost = Area × Rate = 616 × 4.5

Cost = 616 × (9/2) = 308 × 9 = ₹2772

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2772.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the sphere (r) = 7 cm

Rate of painting = ₹4.5 per cm²

π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area of Sphere = 4 × π × r²

Total Cost = Surface Area × Rate per unit area

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0331013a402bb9712b5748ca48299fef2f04cc380371c94ac8f2d3f439355278.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × (22/7) × 7 × 7

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × 22 × 7

⇒ Surface Area = 88 × 7 = 616 cm²

⇒ Total Cost = 616 × 4.5

⇒ Total Cost = 616 × (45/10)

⇒ Total Cost = 616 × (9/2)

⇒ Total Cost = 308 × 9

⇒ Total Cost = ₹2772

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2772.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Sphere

The volume of a sphere is given by the formula V = (4/3) × π × r³.

Hemisphere Formulas

Curved Surface Area = 2πr² | Total Surface Area = 3πr² | Volume = (2/3)πr³.

Surface Area Comparison

A sphere has the minimum surface area for a fixed volume compared to any other shape.

questions.question: Mohan and Sohan invested Rs. 3,000 and Rs. 4,000 respectively in a property and after 6 month Sohan withdraws. If in the end of the year their profit is Rs. 540, then what is the profit earned by Mohan?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Mohan's investment: Rs. 3,000

Sohan's investment: Rs. 4,000

Sohan's time of investment: 6 months

Total profit at the end of the year: Rs. 540

**Concept: **The profit is distributed according to the ratio of the product of investment and time.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Mohan's share in the investment = 3000 × 12 = 36000

⇒ Sohan's share in the investment = 4000 × 6 = 24000

Mohan's share of profit:

⇒ (36000/(36000+24000)) × 540

⇒ Rs. 324

**Therefore, Mohan earned a profit of Rs. 324.**

questions.question: Seats for Engineering, Management and Science in a University are in the ratio of 7 ∶ 8 ∶ 9. There is a proposal to increase these seats by 20%, 30% and 60% respectively. What will be the ratio of the increased seats?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Initial ratio of seats for Engineering, Management and Science: 7 : 8 : 9

Proposed increase in seats: 20%, 30%, 60% respectively

**Concept: **To find the new ratio, increase each term in the ratio by its respective percentage and simplify if possible.

**Calculation:**

⇒ New ratio = 7 × (1+20/100) : 8 × (1+30/100) : 9 × (1+60/100)

⇒ 8.4 : 10.4 : 14.4

⇒ 21 : 26 : 36

**Therefore, the ratio of the increased seats is 21 : 26 : 36.**

questions.question: Two trains running in the same direction at 110 km/h and 90 km/h completely pass one another in 54 sec. If the length of the first train is 130 metres, then find the length of the second train.
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Speed of first train: 110 km/h

Speed of second train: 90 km/h

Time taken to cross each other: 54 seconds

Length of first train: 130 meters

**Concept: **The length of the second train equals the relative speed multiplied by the time taken to cross each other, minus the length of the first train.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Convert speeds from km/h to m/s (multiply by 5/18): 30.56 m/s and 25 m/s

⇒ Relative speed = 30.56 - 25 = 5.56 m/s

⇒ Length of second train = 5.56 m/s x 54 seconds - 130 metres = 170 metres

**Therefore, the length of the second train is 170 metres.**

questions.question: A cyclist moving on a circular track of radius 140 m completes one revolution in 2 min. What is the average speed of the cyclist?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Radius of circular track: 140 m

Time taken for one revolution: 2 min

**Concept: **

The average speed is the total distance divided by the total time. For a circular track, the distance for one revolution is the circumference of the circle.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Circumference = 2 × π × r = 2 × 22/7 × 140 m = 880 m

⇒ Average speed = 880 m / 2 min = 440 m/min

**Therefore, the average speed of the cyclist is 440 m/min.**

questions.question: Find the mean proportional of 0.75 and 3?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Two numbers: 0.75 and 3

**Concept:** The mean proportional (geometric mean) of two numbers a and b is √(ab).

⇒ Mean proportional = √(0.75 × 3) = 1.5

**Therefore, the mean proportional of 0.75 and 3 is 1.5.**

questions.question: If a reduction of 10% in the price of rice enables a person to obtain 22 kg more for ₹250, then the original price of rice per kg is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Savings due to price reduction = 10% of ₹250 = ₹25.

This saved amount allows the purchase of the extra 22 kg at the new reduced price.

New price per kg = ₹25 ÷ 22.

Original price per kg = New price ÷ 90% = (25 ÷ 22) × (100 ÷ 90) = 250 ÷ 198.

Original price ≈ ₹1.26.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1.26.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount = ₹250

Reduction in price = 10%

Increase in quantity = 22 kg

**Concept Used:**

When the total expenditure remains constant, Price and Consumption (Quantity) are inversely proportional.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/780edb7551a9bb2e69acd85c7dab7e93ce3adcc87c2dc297091e649b22ff2367.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price Ratio (Original : New) = 100 : 90 = 10 : 9

⇒ Consumption Ratio (Original : New) = 9 : 10

⇒ Increase in consumption ratio = 10 − 9 = 1 unit

⇒ 1 unit = 22 kg

⇒ Original Consumption = 9 units = 9 × 22 = 198 kg

⇒ Original Price = Total Amount ÷ Original Consumption

⇒ Original Price = 250 ÷ 198 = 1.2626... ≈ ₹1.26

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1.26.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Price and Consumption Relation

When total expenditure remains constant, price and consumption are inversely proportional (Price × Consumption = Constant). If price ratio is a : b, consumption ratio becomes b : a.

Base Change Method

If the price of a commodity decreases by x%, the consumption can be increased by (x ÷ (100 − x)) × 100% without increasing the total expenditure.

Successive Percentage Change

The net percentage change formula is a + b + (a × b ÷ 100). This applies when multiple percentage changes occur on a base value successively.

questions.question: The HCF and LCM of 2 numbers are 32 and 192. One of the numbers is 64. Find the absolute difference between the numbers.
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

HCF: 32

LCM: 192

One of the numbers: 64

**Concept:** For two numbers, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM. The absolute difference is the absolute value of the difference between the

two numbers.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Other number = (HCF × LCM)/given number = (32 × 192)/64 = 96

⇒ Absolute difference = |96 - 64| = 32

**Therefore, the absolute difference between the numbers is 32.**

questions.question: The expenses on rice, petrol and oil of a family are in the ratio 8 ∶ 11 ∶ 6. If the prices of these items are increased by 10%, 20% and 30%, respectively, then the total expenses of the family on these items are increased by:
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Ratio of expenses on rice, petrol and oil: 8 : 11 : 6

Increase in prices: 10%, 20%, 30% respectively

**Concept:**

Concept used: Ratio and percentage

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

Total initial ratio = (8 + 11 + 6) = 25.

Then,

8 × 110/100 = 8.80, 11 × 120/100 = 13.20, and 6 × 130/100 = 7.80

Total final ratio = (8.80 + 13.20 + 7.80) = 29.8

Percentage increase in expenses = ((29.8 - 25) / 25) × 100 = 19.2%

questions.question: A school manager decides to build a new school building in 40 days. He employs 100 men in the beginning and 100 men after 35 days and completes the construction within the stipulated time. If he had not employed the additional men, how many days behind schedule would the school building have been completed?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Work done by 100 additional men in the last 5 days = 100 × 5 = 500 man-days.

If no extra men were employed, this remaining work would be done by the initial 100 men.

Extra time needed = 500 ÷ 100 = 5 days.

Thus, the project would be delayed by 5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total stipulated time = 40 days

Initial workforce (M₁) = 100 men

Time they worked alone (D₁) = 35 days

New workforce after 35 days (M₂) = 100 + 100 = 200 men

Time they worked together (D₂) = 40 − 35 = 5 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = (M₁ × D₁) + (M₂ × D₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work required for the building = (100 × 35) + (200 × 5)

⇒ Total work = 3500 + 1000 = 4500 man-days

⇒ If additional men were not employed, the original 100 men would have to complete all 4500 man-days.

⇒ Time required by 100 men = 4500 ÷ 100 = 45 days

⇒ Original scheduled time = 40 days

⇒ Days behind schedule = 45 − 40 = 5 days

**∴ The correct answer is 5 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

MDH Chain Rule

If M₁ men can do W₁ work in D₁ days working H₁ hours per day, and M₂ men can do W₂ work in D₂ days working H₂ hours per day, then (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the work done by individuals. If they work for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.
</p

questions.question: ₹12,000 becomes ₹15,972 in a certain period of time at the rate of 10% per annum on compound interest, compounding annually. Find the period of time.
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Principal amount: ₹12,000

Amount after certain period: ₹15,972

Rate of interest: 10% per annum

**Concept: **The formula for compound interest is A = P(1 + r/n)⁽ⁿt⁾, where:

A = the amount of money accumulated after n years, including interest.

P = the principal amount (the initial amount of money)

r = annual interest rate (decimal)

n = number of times that interest is compounded per year

t = time the money is invested for in years

**Calculation:**

We need to find 't' (time)

⇒ 15972 = 12000(1 + 10/100)t

⇒ 15972/12000 = (1.1)t

⇒ 1331/1000 = (11/10)t

⇒ (11/10)³ = (11/10)t

⇒ t = 3 years

**Therefore, the period of time is 3 years.**

questions.question: The marked price of a hair dryer is Rs. 10,550. The shopkeeper offers a discount of 18% on it. Find its selling price.
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Marked price: Rs. 10,550

Discount: 18%

**Concept: **The selling price is the marked price minus the discount.

**Calculation:**

Selling price = Marked price - Discount

⇒ Rs. 10,550 - 0.18 × Rs. 10,550 = Rs. 8,651

**Therefore, the selling price of the hair dryer is Rs. 8,651.**

questions.question: The marked price of a mobile phone was ₹10,000. The shop owner offered 10% discount but on further request by the customer, he sold it at ₹8500 after giving a cash discount. How much is this cash discount in percentage (up to 2 decimal places)?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Marked price = ₹10,000

Discount = 10% discount

Further discounted price: ₹8500

**Concept: **

The cash discount is the additional discount given after the initial discount, expressed as a percentage of the discounted price.

**Calculation:**

Selling Price after 10% discount = 10000 × 90/100 = Rs. 9000

⇒ Cash discount = ₹9,000 - ₹8,500 = ₹500

⇒ Cash discount in percentage = (₹500 / ₹9,000) × 100 = 5.56%

**Therefore, the cash discount is 5.56%.**
